title: Serotonin transporter occupancy of five selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors at different doses: an [11C]DASB positron emission tomography study
authors: Meyer JH, Wilson AA, Sagrati S, Hussey D, Carella A, Potter WZ, et al.
population: Healthy volunteers given subtherapeutic doses and patients with mood or anxiety disorders given therapeutic doses of citalopram, fluoxetine, sertraline (14 subjects), paroxetine or extended-release venlafaxine, Toronto
funder: Supported by the National Alliance for Research on Schizophrenia and Depression, Eli Lilly Canada, and the Canadian Institutes of Health Research. One author's affiliation is Eli Lilly and Company, Indianapolis.
result: Striatal serotonin transporter occupancy after 4 weeks rose with dose and plasma level along a saturating curve, f(x)=a(x/[b+x]), with substantial occupancy at subtherapeutic doses and a plateau at higher doses; for sertraline the dose fit was f(x)=94(x/[b+x]). Mean occupancy at minimum therapeutic doses (sertraline 50 mg) was 76% to 85%. In 36 depressed subjects occupancy was not related to change in Hamilton score (r=0.20, p=0.24).
